newsitem.title: UK: UK investment watchdog looks to boost standards.
newsitem.headline: UK investment watchdog looks to boost standards.

text.p: IMRO, Britain's watchdog over the investment management industry, unveiled a plan on Monday to raise industry standards and improve investor awareness.

IMRO, which last week slapped a record two million pounds fine Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, said it wants to do more training of regulators, firms and investors and raise industry standards by changing its admissions process.
"Only through knowledge and awareness can the regulator hope to achieve effective investor protection," said IMRO chief executive Phillip Thorpe in a statement.

IMRO said it will improve its admissions process by including a second stage which will mean that most firms will have their activities restricted before they have successfully undergone a first monitoring visit.
The regulator said it hopes to complete a pilot study by the Autumn designed to free resources by devoting less time to firms which pose a low risk to investors.
